details.description: Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v1 is a 34-billion-parameter code-generation model from Phind, fine-tuned from Meta's CodeLlama-34B base model on a proprietary dataset of roughly 80,000 high-quality programming problems and solutions structured as instruction-answer pairs, trained for 2 epochs (about 160,000 total examples). Like Phind's Python-specific variant, it is "somewhat instruction-tuned, but not chat-tuned," so it is meant to be given direct task descriptions rather than conversational prompts. Phind's model card notes the model "has undergone very limited testing" and states Phind has since released Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2, which the same page reports scores higher on HumanEval.
advantages: Scores 67.6% pass@1 on HumanEval, which Phind's model card describes as matching GPT-4's performance on the same benchmark.
Fine-tuned on roughly 80,000 high-quality, instruction-formatted programming problems and solutions, per the model card.
disadvantages: "Somewhat instruction-tuned, but not chat-tuned," per the model card, so it is not designed for multi-turn conversational prompting.
Phind's model card states the model "has undergone very limited testing" and recommends additional safety testing before real-world deployment.
Superseded by Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2, which Phind's own model card reports scores 73.8% pass@1 on HumanEval versus 67.6% for this v1 model.
use_cases: General-purpose code generation from direct task or problem descriptions
Solving programming problems posed as instruction-style prompts

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens (16384) is consistent with the CodeLlama-34B base model's published 16K context length. The model card states a training sequence length of 4096 tokens ("We used a sequence length of 4096 tokens"), which is a fine-tuning detail rather than the model's architectural context window, so it is not restated as a context-length fact. The model card's own note about Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2 (73.8% pass@1) is a maker statement about a successor, not a formal deprecation notice for v1, so it is described as superseded rather than deprecated.
